00002| title: cacheTag
00003| description: Learn how to use the cacheTag function to manage cache invalidation in your Next.js application.
00004| related:
00005|   title: Related
00006|   description: View related API references.
00007|   links:
00008|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
00009|     - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
00010|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
00011|     - app/api-reference/functions/updateTag
00012|     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
00013| ---
00014| 
00015| The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
00016| 
00017| ## Usage
00018| 
00019| To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
00020| 
00021| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
00022| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00023| 
00024| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00025|   cacheComponents: true,
00026| }
00027| 
00028| export default nextConfig
00029| ```
00030| 
00031| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
00032| const nextConfig = {
00033|   cacheComponents: true,
00034| }
00035| 
00036| export default nextConfig
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
00040| 
00041| ```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
00042| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00043| 
00044| export async function getData() {
00045|   'use cache'
00046|   cacheTag('my-data')
00047|   const data = await fetch('/api/data')
00048|   return data
00049| }
00050| ```
00051| 
00052| ```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
00053| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00054| 
00055| export async function getData() {
00056|   'use cache'
00057|   cacheTag('my-data')
00058|   const data = await fetch('/api/data')
00059|   return data
00060| }
00061| ```
00062| 
00063| You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
00064| 
00065| - Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.
00066| - Use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) when it is acceptable to serve stale data while revalidation happens in the background, or when revalidating from a [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or other context.
00067| 
00068| For example, this Server Function adds a post and then purges every cache entry tagged `'my-data'` so the next read reflects the change:
00069| 
00070| ```tsx filename="app/action.ts" switcher
00071| 'use server'
00072| 
00073| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00074| 
00075| export default async function submit() {
00076|   await addPost()
00077|   updateTag('my-data')
00078| }
00079| ```
00080| 
00081| ```jsx filename="app/action.js" switcher
00082| 'use server'
00083| 
00084| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00085| 
00086| export default async function submit() {
00087|   await addPost()
00088|   updateTag('my-data')
00089| }
00090| ```
00091| 
00092| ## Good to know
00093| 
00094| - **Idempotent Tags**: Applying the same tag multiple times has no additional effect.
00095| - **Multiple Tags**: You can assign multiple tags to a single cache entry by passing multiple string values to `cacheTag`.
00096| 
00097| ```tsx
00098| cacheTag('tag-one', 'tag-two')
00099| ```
00100| 
00101| - **Limits**: A single `cacheTag()` call accepts up to 128 tags, each with a maximum length of 256 characters. Tags longer than 256 characters are skipped, and any tags past the 128th in one call are dropped. Both cases log a console warning.
00102| 
00103| ## Examples
00104| 
00105| ### Tagging components or functions
00106| 
00107| Tag your cached data by calling `cacheTag` within a cached function or component:
00108| 
00109| ```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" switcher
00110| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00111| 
00112| interface BookingsProps {
00113|   type: string
00114| }
00115| 
00116| export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) {
00117|   'use cache'
00118|   cacheTag('bookings-data')
00119| 
00120|   async function getBookingsData() {
00121|     const data = await fetch(`/api/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`)
00122|     return data
00123|   }
00124| 
00125|   return //...
00126| }
00127| ```

00129| ```jsx filename="app/components/bookings.js" switcher

00147| You can use the data returned from an async function to tag the cache entry.

00027| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'

00029| export async function getProducts() {

00033| }

00036| `cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object:

00038| | Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |
00039| | --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- |
00040| | `default` | 5m      | 15m          | never    |

00047|

00051| 'use cache'
00052| cacheLife({
00053|   stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
00054|   revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
00055|   expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
00056| })
00057| ```

export async function getAllProducts() {
  'use cache'
  cacheTag('products')

  // Simulate database delay
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100))

  return [
    { id: 1, name: 'Laptop', price: 999 },

    { id: 3, name: 'Tablet', price: 499 },

    { id: 5, name: 'Watch', price: 299 },
  ]
}
